issue_context.title: node Event missing apiVersion in the involvedObject
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

I'm attempting to use an `Events` watcher to better re-act to cluster modifications. I've received the below event:

```
{ 
   "metadata":{ 
      "name":"172.26.64.24.15ec9789b5157656",
      "namespace":"default",
      "selfLink":"/api/v1/namespaces/default/events/172.26.64.24.15ec9789b5157656",
      "uid":"28bf0748-3a6e-4590-8c4e-1f262ebb7519",
      "resourceVersion":"107982651",
      "creationTimestamp":"2020-01-23T18:29:49Z"
   },
   "involvedObject":{ 
      "kind":"Node",
      "name":"172.26.64.24",
      "uid":"bb6bd832-895d-11e8-bd5a-001d0917d583"
   },
   "reason":"RegisteredNode",
   "message":"Node 172.26.64.24 event: Registered Node 172.26.64.24 in Controller",
   "source":{ 
      "component":"node-controller"
   },
   "firstTimestamp":"2020-01-23T18:29:47Z",
   "lastTimestamp":"2020-01-23T18:29:47Z",
   "count":1,
   "type":"Normal",
   "eventTime":null,
   "reportingComponent":"",
   "reportingInstance":""
}
```

**What you expected to happen**:

I would expect the `involvedObject` to include `apiVersion` attribute. Not sure if it's all node events or just this particular one.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.16
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: bare metal, rancher's rke
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): centos host nodes
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.18, 4.4
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

review_comments: I'm not an expert on the k8s api versioning... but just want to check there isn't a risk that the `APIVersion` will increase but we will forget to update this hard coded reference? Is there a constant we can refer to, or method call we can use which will guarantee this value stays up to date?
I searched over the codebase and I see that often APIVersion is omitted.

This is sorta related to the nodeRef not being a real node object in the Kubelet. I think this patch is ok, but it definitely should be refactored at some point.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L531-L533
